result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.bipartite_modularity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score a partition of a bipartite graph by Barber's bipartite modularity. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.bipartite_modularity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Score a partition of a bipartite graph by Barber's bipartite modularity. title: >- [Graph.bipartite_modularity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Score a partition of a bipartite graph by Barber's bipartite modularity. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Score a partition of a bipartite graph by Barber's bipartite modularity. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L35781-L35877){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.bipartite_modularity( communities, top_nodes=None, resolution=1.0, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bipartite modularity](../assets/graphs/bipartite-modularity.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Customers Ann, Bob, Cy and Dee on top and the products tea, jam, nails and glue below, split into the partition you pass: Ann, Bob, tea and jam (teal) and Cy, Dee, nails and glue (violet). Only Bob to glue crosses. The null model only joins customers to products: each community scores its share of the 8 edges minus its customer degrees times its product degrees over 8², 4/8 - 5 x 4/64 and 3/8 - 3 x 4/64, 0.1875 each, for a bipartite modularity of 0.375." width="100%"} Ordinary modularity (see `modularity()`) compares a partition against random graphs in which any two nodes may be joined, which misjudges bipartite networks such as users and items, authors and papers, or genes and diseases, where edges only ever run between the two sides. Barber's bipartite modularity (2007) uses a null model with edges only between the sides: `Q_B = Σ_c [ L_c / m - γ k_c d_c / m² ]` where `L_c` is the number of edges inside community `c`, `k_c` and `d_c` are the sums of the degrees of its top-side and bottom-side nodes, and `m` is the number of edges. Communities usually mix nodes from both sides. On a weighted graph (`Graph(weighted=True)`) edge weights replace edge counts. The results match NetworkX's `bipartite.modularity()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name} : The partition to score, given like the `communities=` argument of `modularity()`: the name of a node attribute holding community labels, a dictionary mapping node IDs or labels to community labels, or a list of node groups. Every node must belong to exactly one community. [top_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional list of the nodes on one side (IDs or labels); all other nodes form the other side. If `None` (default), the sides are found by 2-coloring each connected component. The choice only matters when a community spans several components, since flipping the sides of one component changes how its nodes pair up with the rest of the community. [resolution]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The resolution parameter `γ`, as in `modularity()`. Default is `1.0`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The bipartite modularity of the partition, at most `1`. A graph without edges scores `0`. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or not bipartite, `top_nodes=` does not split it into two sides, a node is missing from the partition or appears in two groups, or a label or attribute does not exist. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two groups of customers and the products they buy: grouping each customer with their products scores well, while lumping everything together scores `0`: ::: {#e8bb3e6d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["Ann", "Bob", "Cy", "Dee", "tea", "jam", "nails", "glue"]) .add_edges([("Ann", "tea"), ("Ann", "jam"), ("Bob", "tea"), ("Bob", "jam"), ("Cy", "nails"), ("Cy", "glue"), ("Dee", "glue"), ("Bob", "glue")]) ) split = [["Ann", "Bob", "tea", "jam"], ["Cy", "Dee", "nails", "glue"]] ( round(graph.bipartite_modularity(split, top_nodes=["Ann", "Bob", "Cy", "Dee"]), 3), graph.bipartite_modularity([graph.get_node_ids()]), ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (0.375, 0.0) ``` ::: :::
